title: Bounded decision-tree depth yields a narrow, clean CNF
statement: Let $f\colon (\mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \bbf_2) \to \{0,1\}$ be a Boolean function on $n$ variables, and let $d$ be a natural number. If the decision-tree depth of $f$ is at most $d$, then there is a CNF formula $\psi$ that computes $f$ (that is, $\psi(x) = f(x)$ for every assignment $x$) and whose width is at most $d$, meaning every clause has at most $d$ literals. Moreover $\psi$ can be taken clean: within each clause no literal is repeated, and no two literals share the same underlying variable.
